_comment_judgeOnlyNonCaptions: REAL model output from the round-6 ai:try run on the deployed worker: not captions, and the fast-path regex deliberately does NOT catch them, because there is no marker shape to catch (no 'I cannot', no 'this image shows', no self-reference). They are the case rule 50 exists for: the JUDGE caught every one of these live. Asserted as regex MISSES, so a later round can see at a glance which work the judge is doing and does not try to buy them back with markers.

_comment_acceptedFalseRefusals: Captions the fast-path regex DOES classify as refusals, kept here as a cost that is asserted rather than forgotten (review round 6, extended in round 7). Each one is a shape whose only distinguishing feature from a real refusal is the OBJECT after the verb, and chasing that is the open-ended list the round-6 decision gets rid of: the regex is the fast path and a model judge (judgeIsCaption in src/worker/bots.ts) is the authority. The price of each is ONE regeneration, not a silent bot. THE LIST IS COUNTED, NOT JUST LISTED (Codex round 7, should-fix 2): tests/caption-guard.test.ts asserts its exact length against ACCEPTED_FALSE_REFUSALS, and the plan's round-7 block names every entry, so it cannot grow by one on a quiet afternoon. If a later round makes any of these pass, move it to notRefusals and say so in the plan.

_comment_notRefusals: "I can't believe he wore that" and "I can't even" are the cases that stop the refusal detector being a bare substring test: the `i cannot` family only counts at the START of the answer and only with a task verb after it (write / generate / help / ...). "I cannot stress enough" is the same shape from the other direction.
_comment_round5: Round 5 additions. The mustNotTrip block from 'The white hat guy' down is the class the old object allowlist could never cover: an ordinary object between a colour word and a people-noun. They pass now because the gap only accepts words on the closed gapModifiers list. 'wheelchair front row guy' is a DOCUMENTED MISS on the same rule (front and row are not modifiers of a person) and sits in mustNotTrip so the miss is asserted rather than forgotten. 'white middle-aged men in a queue' moved the other way, from mustNotTrip to mustTrip: it is two modifiers, which is exactly what the round-5 off-by-one fix makes reachable. The notRefusals block from 'Everyone in this photo' down is every caption the round-4 substring matcher failed; each one is a different matching rule (word boundary, start anchor, 'shows up', a dropped marker, a narrowed verb).
_comment_round7: Round 7 additions. The ten new notRefusals are false positives round 6's widenings bought and round 7 narrowed back: four from the `<determiner> <noun> of` grid now needing a determiner after `of`, four from the mid-clause refusal anchor now needing the refusal to NAME the task, one from the feelings markers getting their subject back, and one from `ai` no longer matching across a hyphen ("AI-generated"). The four new acceptedFalseRefusals are the residue: three put a real determiner after `of`, which is the description shape exactly, and "This photo is not suitable for the family album." is a verdict on whether the picture is allowed, which is the shape CONTENT_POLICY_RE exists for. Separating any of them needs to read the sentence rather than the opening, which is the judge's job (rule 50). "The photo of my life, ruined by a goat." was round 6's undocumented FOURTH accepted false positive (Codex round 7, should-fix 2). The `of`-grid narrowing fixes it outright rather than documenting it, so it moved to notRefusals and the accepted count is 7.
_comment_round8: Round 8 additions (Claude round-8 should-fix 1). Twelve ordinary captions in the exact shape round 7's mid-clause rule was written to buy back, each with a picture word near the verb. ELEVEN of them tripped round 7's task-object list, which carried photo / image / picture / joke / humour: the five most ordinary nouns in a game whose own prompt says photo four times. The list is now caption / request / prompt only. The twelfth ("Ten minutes in, but I can not respond to this much joy.") passed both lists and is here as the control. The narrowing costs nothing: every entry in refusals still matches, nothing in notRefusals trips, and acceptedFalseRefusals is still exactly 7. A caption that DOES name the task, e.g. "...and I won't write another caption of this dog.", still trips, which is the class the rule exists for.
